predicate.label: trailed sporting competitor
predicate.definition: Sporting competitor X was behind competitor Y in a game score or competitive standings.
includes: explicit lower score or standings position relative to Y
excludes: a completed defeat without evidence of trailing during play or in standings
X leading or ahead of Y
ambiguous: a generic behind phrase without competitive context
a proposed or hypothetical score situation
predicate.notes: Trailing is an intermediate state and does not imply the final winner. The direction is trailing competitor to leading competitor.
predicate.scope_notes: Includes: explicit trail or games-behind; explicit lower score or standings position relative to Y; historical in-game or season standings. Excludes: a completed defeat without evidence of trailing during play or in standings; political or commercial ranking; ordinary following or geographic movement; X leading or ahead of Y. Ambiguous unless resolved by case-local evidence: a generic behind phrase without competitive context; unclear ordered competitor roles; a proposed or hypothetical score situation. Trailing is an intermediate state and does not imply the final winner. The direction is trailing competitor to leading competitor.

rationale: Trailing opponent has eight rows versus sweep/victory seven, so intermediate score/standings lag is the dominant primary predicate; being swept does not itself prove a specified trailing snapshot.
